Final Project: Grammy Award for Record of the Year

TESTS FOR MY PROJECT

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
roty_data <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cheiderman/JOUR405/refs/heads/main/project/JOUR405%20Final%20Project%20Data%20ROTY%20-%20data.csv")
```

***H1 (lyric count): Records with higher total lyric count are more likely to win the Grammy Award for Record of the Year. ***
Compare lyrics between winners and non-winners
Two sample T-test to compare lyric length and songs that won
Test: Two sample T-test
DV: is_winner (0 = non-winner, 1 = winner)
DV: lyric_count

```{r}
roty_data <- roty_data|>
  mutate(
    is_winner = as.numeric(is_winner))
```

```{r}
table(roty_data$is_winner)
```


```{r}
roty_data |>
  summarize(
    mean_lyrics = mean(lyric_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_lyrics = sd(lyric_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n()
  )
```

```{r}
t.test(
  roty_data$lyric_count[roty_data$is_winner == 1],
  roty_data$lyric_count[roty_data$is_winner == 0],
  alternative = "greater",
  var.equal = FALSE)
```

##My understanding of the results
-Mean lyric count for non-winners (0) is  425.4161
-Mean lyric count for winners (1) is 359.8519
-T-statistic is -1.7663. The negative value tells me that winners had a lower average lyric count than non-winners
-P-value is 0.08569. Because the p-value is more than 0.05, the test did not yield statistically significant evidence that the average lyric count differs between winners and non-winners. 


######

***H2 (BPM): Records with a faster average BPM are more likely to win the Grammy Award for Record of the Year than other nominees.*** 
Compare BPM between winners and non-winners
Two sample T-test to compare song BPM and songs that won. 
Test: Two sample T-test
IV: is_winner (0 = non-winner or 1 = winner)
DV: song BPM

```{r}
roty_data <- roty_data|>
  mutate(
    is_winner = as.numeric(is_winner))
```

```{r}
table(roty_data$is_winner)
```


```{r}
roty_data |>
  summarize(
    mean_lyrics = mean(bpm, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_lyrics = sd(bpm, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n()
  )
```

```{r}
t.test(
  roty_data$bpm[roty_data$is_winner == 1],
  roty_data$bpm[roty_data$is_winner == 0],
  alternative = "greater",
  var.equal = FALSE)
```
##My understanding of the results
-Mean bpm for non-winners (0) is  123.8759
-Mean bpm for winners (1) is 113.8519
-T-statistic is -1.8395. The negative value tells me that winners had a lower BPM count than non-winners.
-P-value is 0.07239. Because the p-value is more than 0.05, the test did not yield statistically significant evidence that the average bpm differs between winners and non-winners. 


#######

***H3 (Key): Songs in major keys are more likely to win the Grammy Award for Record of the Year than songs in minor keys. ***
Are more ROTY winners major or minor modes?
Test: Chi-squared of independence
IV: mode (major/minor)
DV: is_winner (winner/non-winner)

```{r}
mode_table <- table(roty_data$mode, roty_data$is_winner)
```
```{r}
mode_table
```

```{r}
chisq.test(mode_table)
```

```{r}
roty_data |>
  group_by(mode) |>
  summarize(
    total_songs = n(),
    winner = sum(is_winner),
    win_percent = mean(is_winner) * 100
  )
```

##My understanding of the results
-The p-value is 0.05711, which is just slightly above 0.05. It is very close to statistical significant results.

***Are some songs more likely to win the Grammy Award for Song of the Year then others?***

Reason behind the project: I am a huge music lover and look forward to watching the Grammy's each year. I love making my own predictions ahead of the awards, but have never had a formal reason behind my picks beside my personal opinions. I am curious to learn if there are specific characteristics of songs that can make them more likely to win ROTY beyond the quality of production/lyrics/chart performance. 

Research question: If we compare the songs nominated for the ROTY Grammy Award since 1990, can we determine if certain characteristics make the record more likely to win? 

***H1 (lyric count): Records with higher total lyric count are more likely to win the Grammy Award for Record of the Year. ***
---For this hypothesis, I will count total words including repeated choruses. To find this data, I will use https://wordcounter.io/ to manually check the number of lyrics in each song---

***H2 (BPM): Records with a faster BPM of 120 are more likely to win the Grammy Award for Record of the Year than other nominees.*** 
---For this hypothesis, I will group songs by 30 beats to organize BPM. Songs will most likely fall between 60 and 180 BPM. I will use Tunebat to determine the BPM. ---

***H3 (Key): Songs in major keys are more likely to win the Grammy Award for Record of the Year than songs in minor keys. ***
---For this hypothesis, I will determine song key for each nominee using Tunebat.----

To test these hypothesos, I can examine all of the songs nominated since 1990 for SOTY. I can determine if the number of lyrics, the BPM, and the key can make a record more likely to win over others. From these findings, I hope to see a trend on why certain songs might win over others. 

Data: For this project, I can will use official data from the Recording Academy to determine the list of nominees and winners for each year (1990-present). I will determine BPM and key from Tubebat. I will use https://wordcounter.io/ to count the number of lyrics. 


***Link to CSV data:***
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cheiderman/JOUR405/refs/heads/main/project/JOUR405%20Final%20Project%20Data%20ROTY%20-%20data.csv")
```

***Key for my CSV data:***
--year: Year of the Grammy ceremony (1990–2024)
--song_title: Name of the nominated song track
--artist: Name of performing artist
--is_winner: Grouped by 1 and 0. 1 for Record of the Year winners, 0 for nominees.
--lyric_count: Total word count in the lyrics, including repeated choruses
--bpm: Beats per minute
--key: Key letter of the song
--mode: Used to compare Major key vs. Minor key
--key_mode: This will help combine key letter with the mode.
 
**Note, I am still in the process of gathering all of my data.***

The most important columns for my analysis will be lyric_count, bpm, key_mode and is_winner.
